free_tier.stated: 512 MB plan at USD 4.62/month billed USD 27.75 semi-annually: 1 vCPU, 512 MB RAM, 15 GB NVMe, 5 TB transfer, 1.5 Gbps port, IPv4 + IPv6, in Sofia Bulgaria, Stockholm Sweden or Amsterdam Netherlands. It is sold out: the page states "Stock last updated: October 20th, 2026 - More stock soon." and the 512 MB plan reads "Out of stock in all locations". The next size up is 1 GB at USD 7.60/month (USD 22.80 quarterly) with 1 vCPU, 20 GB NVMe, 6 TB and 1.5 Gbps, whose orderability did not test: the out-of-stock line appears inside the 512 MB block and the extract does not pair a stock state with each size.

egress.terms: 5 TB a month on the 512 MB plan, 6 TB on the 1 GB plan, rising with the plan; no overage price published on the page read
egress.free_allowance: 5 TB per month on the 512 MB plan

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with root and NVMe storage, six POPs across the US and Europe, sold through the vendor's own site; no API documented on the page read. The vendor's description states the service is sold with "no personal information required" and accepts cryptocurrency payments, which is a claim about registration that did not verify against a signup form.
chaining: A 1.5 Gbps port and 5 TB a month on three European POPs makes this the best-shaped egress box after Hosting Int., and 512 MB with 15 GB of NVMe runs a tunnel or a DNS node the plan cannot be ordered today, and the 1 GB at USD 7.60 is the nearest thing to a substitute inside the same provider.
